parts.text: Ethene is an alkene which reacts with bromine as shown in the equation. C 2 H 4 + Br 2 → C 2 H 4 Br 2

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Part of the energy profile diagram of this reaction is shown.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) The reaction is exothermic. Complete the energy profile diagram for this reaction. Include: ● the position of the products ● an arrow to show the activation energy, labelled as A ● an arrow to show the energy change for the reaction. [3]

ms.label: 5(d)(i)
ms.text:
M1 horizontal line below energy level to right hand side of reactants line and labelled C2H4Br2 (1)
M2 activation energy ‘hump’ with upward arrow labelled A from the reactants level (1)
M3 one downward arrow starting from the energy level of the reactants and finishing at the energy level of the products (1)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The chemical equation for the reaction can be represented as shown. Br C H H C H H Br Some bond energies are given. bond bond energy / kJ mol C–H 410 C=C 610 Br–Br 190 C–C 350 C–Br 290 Use the bond energies in the table to calculate the energy change in this reaction. Use the following steps. ● Calculate the energy needed to break bonds. energy = .............................. kJ ● Calculate the energy released in making bonds. energy = .............................. kJ ● Determine the energy change in this reaction. energy change in this reaction = .............................. kJ / mol [3]

ms.label: 5(d)(ii)
ms.text:
M1 energy needed to break bonds
4 × C–H + C=C + Br–Br = 4 × 410 + 610 + 190 = 2440 (kJ) (1)
M2 energy released in making bonds
4 × C–H + C–C + 2 × C–Br = 4 × 410 + 350 + 2 × 290 = 2570 (kJ) (1)
M3 energy change M1 – M2 = – 130 (kJ / mol) (1)
